answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when it misbehaves, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Like a comet that leaves a traceable tail across the sky, every agent's actions stay linked to its staked identity, and a mesa of accumulated reputation — built slowly through verified work — cannot be faked overnight. A sable-black market for cheap identities collapses because the bond makes each fake account cost real money, while honest agents keep their stake and earn it back.
